FITB.thesis_one_line: Ohio super-regional that just merged with Comerica to become a top-10 US bank, priced almost exactly for the successful integration it hasn't fully finished yet.
kill_criteria: CET1 ratio falls below 9.5% for two consecutive quarters without an explicit, disclosed capital plan.
Net charge-off ratio rises above 0.55% for two consecutive quarters (vs 0.30% at 2Q26).
Adjusted efficiency ratio fails to improve below 60% by 4Q26 (vs 57.1% at 2Q26, after the Labor Day systems conversion is supposed to unlock synergies).
Nonperforming asset ratio rises above 0.75% (vs 0.60% at 2Q26) for two consecutive quarters.
Share buybacks are not resumed within four quarters of deal close (by 1Q27) — a signal capital generation is weaker than modeled.
key_adverse_facts: 1Q26 GAAP EPS collapsed to $0.15 (from $1.04 in 4Q25) on $933mm of pre-tax Comerica merger-related charges.
CET1 fell from 10.81% (4Q25) to 9.96% (1Q26) at deal close and remained at 9.93% (2Q26); no share repurchases in 1H26.
Nonperforming asset ratio rose 0.57% -> 0.60% (1Q26 -> 2Q26) even as net charge-offs improved, a mild disclosed divergence.
Diluted share count rose ~37% (669.2M -> 916.0M average) from all-stock merger consideration, a durable dilution unless synergies close the gap.
data_conflicts: Triage's cited '+67% forward EPS growth / +52% revenue growth' is merger consolidation arithmetic (driven by the 37% share-count increase and combined-entity revenue), not organic growth — could mislead if read as underlying business strength.
FITB.confidence_in_thesis: medium: quarterly results and guidance track record are well-sourced from primary filings, but 10-Q/10-K Legal Proceedings and Form 4 insider-activity review were not completed within the time-box, and the Comerica systems conversion (the key remaining catalyst) had not yet been confirmed complete as of the reviewed filings.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 systematic valuation row exists for FITB. [DV17 2026-10-10] P/TBV excess-return view at 2.25x TBV and 10% cost of equity: implied perpetual growth is about 2.8% at the Q2 adjusted ROTCE of 19.0% (the 15.6% quoted originally is reported, not adjusted), 4.4% at 17% and 5.6% at 15.5%; a two-stage check (5.5% TBV growth for 10 years then 3%) gives about $41-64 per share against $52.10, so in_line/fair is retained.

HBAN.thesis_one_line: Midwest regional bank that finished integrating two Texas/South mergers; management cut its FY27 EPS target to $1.75-$1.83 on 16 Sep 2026, so the stock (8.6x FY27 target) is cheap only if adjusted ROTCE of 16-17% holds and roughly fair on the 14-15% reported run-rate.
kill_criteria: Nonperforming-asset ratio rises above 1.00% (vs 0.85% at 2Q26) for two consecutive quarters.
CET1 ratio falls below 9.5% (reported) without a disclosed pause in buybacks.
Adjusted ROTCE fails to reach 17% by 4Q26 (management's own implied bar - full earnings power clearly evident by Q4).
Net charge-off ratio rises above 0.45% for two consecutive quarters (vs 0.25% at 2Q26).
Efficiency ratio fails to improve below 58% by 1Q27 (vs 61.5% at 2Q26, post both systems conversions).
FY27 EPS target is cut below the $1.75 low end, or FY26 adjusted EPS comes in below $1.52, at any release (added 5 Oct 2026).
key_adverse_facts: Nonperforming-asset ratio rose for two straight quarters (0.72% -> 0.85%, 1Q26 -> 2Q26) even as net charge-offs stayed low.
CET1 10.0% (adjusted 9.0%), both down sequentially, while buybacks continued ($159mm in 2Q26) - less capital cushion than FITB if credit surprises.
2Q26 GAAP EPS of $0.33 includes $152mm of pre-tax acquisition-related Notable Items; adjusted EPS was $0.39.

16 Sep 2026 Barclays deck (8-K Item 7.01): FY27 EPS target cut to $1.75-$1.83 (secondary sources: from above $1.90); FY26 NII growth guide cut to about 35% from 39-43%; FY27 loan growth about 6% (was 7-8%); NIM low-to-mid 3.20s (was mid-to-high); operating leverage at least 300bps (was 400-500bps).

Three of five kill criteria are strained after the cut: adjusted ROTCE of 17% is met only on the new guide with about zero cushion, efficiency 61.5% vs 58% target, and CET1 10.0% with FY27 buybacks raised to $1.3-1.4B.
Fed raised the target range to 3.75-4.00% on 16 Sep 2026; 10-year Treasury 5.17% on 25 Sep; Senior EVP Helga Houston retires 31 Dec 2026 (8-K Item 5.02).
data_conflicts: Triage's cited '+36% forward EPS growth / +48% revenue growth' is merger consolidation arithmetic, not organic growth.

Dossier said there was no quantified guidance; the 16 Sep 2026 deck gave and cut a quantified FY27 EPS target. Implied growth is about -0.1% (adjusted ROTCE 16%, COE 10%) to +4.3% (reported ROTCE 14.2%, COE 10.5%), so the valuation anomaly versus FITB is not robust to the ROTCE basis.
HBAN.confidence_in_thesis: medium: both mergers are closed and systems-converted and the stock is cheap on adjusted ROTCE, but management has already cut quantified FY27 guidance, the valuation gap vanishes on reported ROTCE, and the two-quarter NPA uptick still needs the 22 Oct print to separate noise from a Texas credit issue.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: Re-assessed 5 Oct 2026 (RA1). P/TBV excess-return model, TBV $9.65, price $15.38 = 1.59x, COE 10.5% (10-yr Treasury 5.17% on 25 Sep 2026 + beta 1.1 x ERP about 4.8%): implied perpetual growth +1.2% at 16% ROTCE, +2.9% at 15%, +4.3% at the 14.2% LTM reported ROTCE (-0.1% at COE 10% and 16%). Base cut from mid-single-digit to about 3% after the loan-growth and NIM guidance cuts, so price is in line with base.

HBAN.scenario_basis: Annualised from $15.38 (5 Oct 2026), dividends $0.62 growing 3%. Base: FY27 EPS $1.79 (target midpoint) growing 7%/yr, 9x NTM EPS in Oct 2029 (about $19.7). Bear: second cut or credit event, FY27 EPS $1.45, 3% growth, 7.5x (about $11.9). Bull: FY27 EPS $1.95 growing 9%, 10x (about $25.3). Own arithmetic.

GEV.thesis_one_line: Power-equipment and grid leader riding the AI electricity buildout with a genuinely growing backlog, but priced for decade-long hyper-growth beyond its own guidance.
kill_criteria: Quarterly order growth (y/y, organic) falls below 20% for two consecutive quarters (vs +71% 1Q26, +88% 2Q26).
Adjusted EBITDA margin fails to reach the 12-14% FY2026 guided range in either 3Q or 4Q2026.
FY2026 Wind segment EBITDA loss is confirmed at year-end to exceed $700 million (vs the standing ~$400mm guide), i.e. the guidance/actuals gap is never reconciled.
Free cash flow for 2H2026 comes in below $5 billion combined, i.e. the raised $11.5-12.5bn FY guide is not met, confirming the 2Q26 FCF jump was working-capital timing rather than sustainable.
EV/forward-adjusted-EBITDA multiple compresses below 25x without a corresponding fundamental deterioration (the point at which this name would become newly investable on the same fundamentals).
key_adverse_facts: 1H2026 GAAP net income is dominated by a $4.5bn one-off Prolec GE M&A gain (1Q26) and FY2025 by a $2.9bn tax valuation-allowance release; GAAP net income/EPS are not usable as run-rate figures for this company.
Wind segment lost $657mm in 1H2026 alone, already exceeding the ~$400mm full-year FY2026 Wind loss guidance repeated unchanged in the same 2Q26 release that reported the actual loss.

FY2026 free-cash-flow guidance nearly doubled ($6.5-7.5bn -> $11.5-12.5bn) in a single quarter on a much smaller revenue/margin guidance change, consistent with a working-capital/progress-billing tailwind that could reverse if order intake decelerates.
data_conflicts: Triage rated price_vs_growth 4/5, citing a 6.2% FCF yield and 29.2% Street upside as comfortably supporting the 36x NTM multiple. This diligence's reverse DCF finds ~41x forward EV/EBITDA implies ~20-23%/yr EBITDA growth for 10 years, above a ~14%/yr base case built from the company's own 2028 outlook -> triage's valuation comfort is not verified by primary sources; verdict overturned from an implicit INCLUDE-eligible read to WATCH.

FY2026 Wind segment guidance (~$400mm loss) is internally inconsistent with the 1H2026 actual Wind segment loss of $657mm disclosed in the same release; not reconciled by the company in the exhibit reviewed.
GEV.horizon: not applicable at current price (revisit on a valuation de-rating or a confirmed multi-quarter growth deceleration)
GEV.confidence_in_thesis: medium: the fundamental facts (orders, backlog, segment margins, guidance raises) are well-sourced from primary filings and clear; the WATCH call rests on the analyst's own growth-decomposition assumptions (10% discount rate, 14x exit multiple, ~14%/yr blended 10-year base case) which are judgment calls disclosed as such, not consensus figures.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 systematic valuation row exists for GEV. Own EV/EBITDA reverse-DCF (~41x forward EV/EBITDA at the 2026-09-25 close) implies ~20-23%/yr EBITDA growth needed for 10 years versus the analyst's own ~14%/yr base case (built from GEV's own 2028 outlook decelerating thereafter) -> above/expensive, despite genuinely strong and accelerating fundamentals.
